sections.title: Carnivorous epiphyte
sections.text: This tropical bladderwort grows in wet habitats, often in water-filled bromeliad leaf axils. Its leaf-like organs carry suction bladders that trap tiny aquatic prey. Flowering scapes can reach about 1 m; the violet flowers may be up to 7.5 cm wide. The illustration’s flowers and inset trap are apt.

sections.title: Habitat and feeding
sections.text: Native to southern Venezuela, Guyana and northern Brazil. It obtains nutrients from small organisms captured in its bladders; the plant is not documented as a food crop.
